Derive columns of a server-side omop.table

Source: R/verbs_v2.R
ds.omop.mutate.Rd

Adds or replaces columns of a server-side, token-keyed data frame with R expressions over its columns, evaluated on every server by the closed mutation grammar of omopMutateDS (design section 2.11): bare names are columns (of the input or assigned earlier in the same call); literals are numbers (5L is an integer), strings, TRUE/FALSE, NA and as.Date("YYYY-MM-DD"); operators are + - * / (division by zero or a non-finite result gives NA; date - date gives days, date +/- integer a date), conditions (== != < <= > >= %in% is.na() ! & |, three-valued: NA when unknown, each comparing one column with one literal), ifelse(test, yes, no), case_when(cond ~ value, ..., .default = ) (an unknown condition gives NA), coalesce(...) and cut(x, breaks, labels, right) (R's right = TRUE default; text labels, NA outside the breaks; breaks/labels may name vectors of your session). Integer arithmetic uses exact signed 64-bit storage when needed; results beyond the ordinary R integer range are retained, and checked 64-bit overflow yields typed NA. Branches and coalescing preserve integer64 and datetime values. Repeated explicit cut labels group their intervals. Nothing is evaluated as R code, on the client or on the server.

Usage

ds.omop.mutate(x = NULL, ..., newobj = NULL, symbol = "omop", conns = NULL)

Arguments

x

Name of the server-side omop.table symbol (default: the session's most recent output).

...

Named expressions, name = expression.

newobj

Name of the symbol to create (default: a fresh name); newobj = x replaces x.

symbol

Session symbol (default "omop").

conns

DSI connections (default: the session's).

Value

Invisibly, the name of the server-side symbol.

Details

Person, episode and set keys and protected columns can be neither read nor written. Class-1 source and assignment names are also refused, even when the administrator permits their direct projection. The result is a released object: its distinct persons must reach the server's nfilter.subset (the server refuses it otherwise, with its constant message) and it carries no differential-privacy provenance. With newobj = x the target is replaced in place on every server; a rollback copy is kept until every server has succeeded, so a failure on one server restores the original everywhere. If restoration cannot be confirmed, the error names the unresolved sites and the retained recovery symbol. A cleanup error after confirmed commit states that the mutation committed and identifies the remaining backup cleanup. Every participating server must publish the dsOMOP 2.10.3 publication protocol and omopMutateDS, and advertise verb.mutate. The client checks this before any assignment, including a rollback copy; an old server or an incomplete published profile refuses the whole call.

See also

ds.omop.filter, ds.omop.select

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
ds.omop.mutate("D_cov", pdc = covered / observed,
               adherent = ifelse(pdc >= 0.8, 1L, 0L),
               age_band = cut(age, c(0, 18, 65, 120), right = FALSE))
} # }
